speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the nature of your rash; can you describe its appearance and where it first appeared? When did these symptoms start, and have you experienced any fever or weight loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the recent onset of a cough alongside your new arthritis management, are you currently taking any specific medications for your joint pain or blood pressure? Also, does the rash appear as small red spots or patches, and have you noticed any joint swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I don't see how iron deficiency anemia would cause a rash, cough, or mucositis; those symptoms strongly suggest a drug eruption or infection instead. Please tell me the exact names of all medications you are taking for your arthritis and cough. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood and metabolic panels are normal, which rules out severe infection or organ failure, but they do not explain the rash, cough, or mucositis. Since you mentioned starting a new medication for arthritis, can you name the specific drug? Also, does the rash on your back itch or burn, and have you noticed any peeling or blistering? REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_photo, Oral_mucosa_photo.

text: Past medical history: Has been diagnosed with arthritis. No other significant past medical history has been mentioned. Social history: The patient didn't provide any specific social history details during the initial consultation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to recent initiation of an arthritic medication.
